lead: you have been the new person four times, and each time the room took eleven weeks to form a view of you. you had the whole of them by the second friday, and you have it still.
sun: most people amend a first impression for four years — the afternoon he was decent about money, the winter she got through better than anybody — and every amendment comes from still being in the room. you are not still in the room. the town goes former in a fortnight, entire, and the version of each person in it stops at whatever you took off them early and stays there.
moon: nothing you took is released, and the strongest holds in you are on people who never became anything. the man who interviewed you in a city you no longer enter — what his voice did before he named the salary — is exact, and he could not pick you out of two. what survives a turning here attaches to whoever you looked at hardest, not to whoever knew you.
pull: the people you know best are strangers from towns you will not enter again. they could not describe you. you could describe the week they stopped enjoying their job.
tension: someone tells you, kindly, in the second year, that you had made your mind up about the department before you met half of it. the finding is accurate. what produced it was a beat of hesitation and a greeting that came in late, and none of that survives being said at a table. no long acquaintance stands against it either, since you will have finished the whole life before anyone could say you were right about the others.
cost: you can walk into a place where nobody owes you anything and know inside a fortnight who is safe and who is the problem, and act on it, and be right. no one is read twice. everyone in your keeping is held at the resolution of a stranger, and whoever improved after you left improved in a life you had finished with.

lead: three complete versions of you have signed the same letterhead. the place has recorded none of them, because a carved chair does not take an impression, and what you were handed was the chair.
sun: a molting needs something that grew on you. the position did not grow. it was carved before you arrived and will be here after, so your endings take only what carries your own name — the trade you actually practise inside the job, the convictions, the household, the person who accepted the offer at twenty-nine. the place registers none of it, having never been in the part that ends.
moon: the bearing comes through every turn without a mark on it — same distance held, same face on the worst mornings — so what the building has watched for twenty years is one continuous person. the private question sharpens with each pass. everything you built has been taken down by you, on purpose, at the root. the item still standing is the one that was standing when you got here.
pull: you have demolished everything you ever made. the one thing still upright is the one that was upright before you arrived, and the room dates your character from it.
tension: continuity is the word they use about you, offered as the reason the place has held together. what it describes is three complete strangers under one signature. producing that would land as a resignation rather than honesty, and the asset this building actually runs on is a belief that one judgment has occupied the seat throughout. so the account stays unsaid, and the people who advanced you advanced somebody they met once.
cost: the place gets an unbroken line of custody, and a decade can pass under you with nothing rearranged below on account of what happened to you. you can finish a whole self on a wednesday and take the meeting on thursday. what stands in your name is other people's work, maintained. everything you designed yourself came down with the one who designed it, and you took it down.

lead: the thing you are known for finished in you about six years ago, in a single season, completely. the room it gathered still fills, on the same night, and the spread does not record seasons.
sun: the ending went all the way down — not less of it, none of it. and nothing of that reaches an audience, because what an audience receives from here is size, and size is not a report on anybody's state. so the evening runs at its old width, hosted by somebody with no stake in the subject, and the room has never had a better one.
moon: there is no smaller version standing by. the width does not come on for the evening — it is the same in a corridor, on a bad morning, at a funeral — so the ordinary way of announcing that a thing has finished, by doing less of it, is unavailable at source. what the finished thing left is the crowd, and the crowd is owed.
pull: you closed the subject six years ago and the room has grown since. nothing you own can be turned down, so the only person who knows it ended is the one hosting it.
tension: you have said it twice, both times plainly, and both times the room decided you were being modest. a person at full width announcing they have lost interest is heard as a person asking to be argued with, whether they meant it that way or not. so nobody has ever received the sentence as information, the invitations go on being accepted, and the crowd keeps growing around a season that ended without a witness.
cost: a whole appetite of yours can die without costing anyone in the room a thing. nothing folds and nobody has to be let down, because the display carries the entire weight of it and always did. what you turned into afterwards has never been shown to anybody, since it came without width, and width is the only thing this room has ever been able to see.

lead: a woman you have not felt anything for since your twenties still gets the call on the day. a man you loved for nine years does not. nothing in you decided which was which.
sun: nobody around you gets a warning shot. there is no month of being slightly less available, no thinning, no run of cancelled evenings that would let a person work out what is coming — the season holds at full and then the season is not there. so anyone who has watched it happen once starts reading you for signs, and finds none, because the equipment that produces a sign was never fitted.
moon: you have never once been mildly anything. a person is at full weight in here or they are not present, and the register everybody else spends most of a life in — seen sometimes, thought of occasionally, fond of at a distance — has never opened. asked how you feel about the man from the second city, what comes up is the whole of it or a blank.
pull: what ends and what is owed come out of one instrument, both at once, at full, and nothing in you gets to say which of them a person is going to get.
tension: nobody has ever been able to ask you for less. what people want, usually, is a lighter version of the thing — fewer calls, birthdays only, nothing weekly — and there is no such setting to move to. so the request comes out as an ending, because ending is the only other position, and the person asking watches a fifteen-year arrangement go in one sentence and spends years working out what they said.
cost: nothing in your life is running on habit — no arrangement half-meant, no friendship continued because stopping would be awkward, no year spent inside something that finished. everything still standing is at full weight. which of them stands was settled by whichever season a person happened to be in, and the ones you would pick now went out with a weather nobody consulted you about.
